title: Opinion that home ownership is a poor investment
why: Argues houses tie people down and lose value, but offers mostly assertion rather than evidence or analysis.

title: Argument that religion provides practical value
why: Opinion piece defending religion's social function; contains assertion without concrete evidence or explanation.

title: Personal account of losing legacy G Suite
why: Anecdote about a free G Suite shutdown and migration pain; no general lesson beyond personal frustration.

title: Why home robots face brutal cost competition
why: Home robots must beat cheap human labor; early buyers are wealthy, so $5,000 price targets remain far from humanoid costs.

title: Vendor reply on GitLab hosting features
why: Company response mostly pitches paid editions and feature requests; little general technical insight.

title: Rebuttal on gender dynamics and self-defense
why: Opinionated rebuttal about culture and gender with anecdote and assertion; no technical or lasting informational value.

title: Wishlist of antitrust targets for tech firms
why: Opinion list of companies to investigate, offering proposals without analysis of evidence or market mechanics.

title: Partisan examples of voter ID manipulation
why: Politically charged examples of how ID rules could be used to disadvantage voters; opinion rather than informative analysis.

title: Lobsters admin explains a sockpuppet ban
why: Moderation dispute over a ban and invite chain; relevant only to one incident, not broadly instructive.

title: Why zero-confirmation Bitcoin payments can be double-spent
why: Unconfirmed transactions can be replaced via RBF with a conflicting spend, so merchants must wait for block confirmations.

title: Anecdote about forced app updates
why: Frustrating personal story about forced updates blocking a ride-hailing app; complaint without general lesson.

title: Full-text indexes of big dumps fit on laptops
why: A 50-60GB knowledge dump indexes to roughly 1-5GB, so millisecond queries locally are practical; cloud search is convention.

title: Defense of Emacs against cosmetic modernization
why: Opinion arguing that cosmetic changes matter less than code; fairly rhetorical, not technical.

title: Argument that society, not government, should limit speech
why: Opinion on free speech and platform responsibility, drawn from a film analogy; no informative content.

title: First impressions of learning Go
why: Mostly subjective gripes about syntax, generics and tooling; opinions without deeper explanation of design tradeoffs.

title: Why ad blockers depend on Chrome's extension store
why: Chromium-based browsers rely on the Chrome Web Store, so Google rejecting old-API extensions would force rivals to build their own stores.

title: Impressions of Stable Diffusion for artists
why: Enthusiastic opinion about image generation; general observations about artistic knowledge without concrete technical insight.

title: Why low interest rates inflate house prices
why: Buyers are sized to a monthly payment; cheaper loans let lenders push bigger balances, so payment caps push prices up, not down.

title: What makes Facebook's engineering culture distinctive
why: High hiring bar enables autonomy: engineers choose work, no OWNERS gatekeeping, and impact rewards productivity and removing bad code.

title: Opinion on GameStop short squeeze
why: Argues about whether retail traders hurt Wall Street; opinion and rhetoric without substantive mechanism explanation.

title: Argument against responding to bullies with violence
why: Moral opinion about violence and bullying, with rhetorical framing rather than evidence or practical technique.

title: Argument against a cashless society
why: Political and financial opinion against cashless payments; assertions about fees and control without solid evidence.

title: Personal story about remote salary offers
why: Anecdote about a negotiation over remote pay; the lesson is narrow and mostly a grievance.

title: Criticism of early mask guidance messaging
why: Opinion about public health communication during the pandemic; argumentative rather than explanatory.

title: Enthusiast notes on small form-factor PC cases
why: Hobbyist preferences and product mentions for small PC cases; useful to few and largely opinion.

title: Bitcoin's 2017 SegWit user-activated soft fork explained
why: Nodes rejecting non-SegWit-signaling blocks would split the chain; miner opposition made the UASF's success unlikely.

title: Rebuttal that self-made success exists
why: Argumentative response to an article, relying on examples and personal judgment rather than data.

title: Former felon on lasting harm from online crime reports
why: Personal account of how online crime stories affect acquaintances; a meaningful perspective but mostly personal reflection.

title: Argument that anyone can be extraordinary
why: Motivational opinion about combining talents; reflective rather than informative.

title: Speculation on psychological hardship of Mars colonists
why: Speculative opinion about boredom and isolation on Mars; no evidence or data cited.

title: Argument for judging people only by community contributions
why: Opinion on separating personal views from community standing; examples are asserted rather than analyzed.

title: Wish for a unified Linux clipboard and keybindings
why: Complaint about inconsistent clipboard and keybindings on Linux; expresses frustration without technical explanation.

title: Zapier announces its Zappy screen capture tool
why: Product launch announcement describing a free screenshot tool for remote teams; promotional rather than instructive.

title: Why ever-growing code of conduct rules backfire
why: Adding rules after each conflict made newcomers fearful, produced silos, and turned the code of conduct into a power tool.

title: Why intrapreneurship lacks startup equity upside
why: Big-company engineers get salary and capped stock, so extra effort does not correlate with reward the way startup equity does.

title: Why online reviews hit small businesses hardest
why: Reviews spread fast, persist, and get ranked; a few one-stars dominate small businesses' visibility, unlike word of mouth that faded.

title: DevOps teams build tools; dev teams run production
why: A platform team creates deployment tooling for owning dev teams, who get paged for their services, unlike traditional sysops.

title: Frustrations sending patches over email
why: Complaint about git send-email obstacles like blocked ports and tab-mangling; mostly grievance rather than a tested fix.

title: Argument that engineers formalize murky problems
why: Passionate opinion that spreadsheet-built tools create errors; persuasive but largely rhetorical rather than instructive.

title: Hypothesis that online platforms amplify stupidity
why: Speculative opinion that feeds reward stupidity content; the argument is plausible but unsupported by data.

title: Burnout as effort that never pays off
why: Burnout comes from long effort without rewards; vacations don't fix it, but getting a visible win does.

title: Reflections on side projects versus corporate work
why: Personal and opinionated comparison of productivity in side projects and big companies; no concrete method.

title: History of H-1B post-layoff grace periods
why: The 60-day grace window was introduced only recently; earlier rules required laid-off H-1B workers to leave immediately.

title: Reproducing Heartbleed private key theft on nginx
why: Heartbleed leaks server memory; the author reports dumping an nginx private key in one request, with setup steps.

title: Critique of SQL ergonomics and vendor fragmentation
why: Opinion on SQL syntax and vendor differences; examples are useful but the piece mainly argues taste.

title: Why the commenter switched from Linux to macOS
why: Personal preference list about stability, hardware and software support; opinion rather than transferable knowledge.

title: Argument that hackers avoid public-interest careers
why: Moral comparison with liberal arts friends; opinion about careers and motives without evidence.

title: Keeping useful internal tools private
why: Anecdote about hoarding a productivity tool at work; personal choice with no broader lesson.

title: Why crowd investing in startups is risky
why: Most startups fail and media hides it; many small investors complicate capital structure, which can hurt later fundraising.

title: Diet argument from plant toxins and fruit evolution
why: Speculative evolutionary argument about diet presented as fact without evidence; mostly opinion.

title: Commentary on Microsoft versus Apple laptops
why: Opinion about market competition and Apple's priorities; speculative and not technically informative.

title: Criticism of Proctorio's bias and privacy
why: Opinion on proctoring software invading privacy and bias; advocacy rather than explanation of how it works.

title: Why cars may immobilize after seat work
why: Seat-occupancy airbag sensors can enter fault states after seat modification; manufacturers can reset them remotely as a safety feature.

title: Argument against equating internships with serfdom
why: Opinion on politics and labor, with a personal anecdote; persuasive but not informative about technology or science.

title: Defense of a maker and commentary on Shenzhen
why: Praise and commentary about a creator and her videos; personal impressions rather than a transferable lesson.

title: List of things that used to be hard
why: Thread of nostalgic gripes and opinions about how tech has changed; unsupported generalizations, not instructive.

title: Why studios insist on DRM despite its weakness
why: Studios know copy protection is breakable and always leaks, but require DRM from rightsholders as a negotiation condition.

title: Pointer-to-pointer removes linked list special cases
why: Storing the address of the link pointer makes deletion a single assignment, removing the head-versus-middle branch from the code.

title: German court ruling on Facebook's default consent
why: Default-on settings and buried imprint fail explicit informed consent; German law applies regardless of Facebook's Irish-jurisdiction claim.

title: Argument against stay-at-home lockdowns
why: Political opinion comparing country strategies and quoting Franklin; rhetorical rather than evidence-based analysis.

title: Thoughts on DRM in the HTML specification
why: Opinion that DRM is unnecessary in HTML, backed by anecdotes about media companies rather than systematic data.

title: Speculation on China's nuclear build-out versus wind and solar
why: Opinionated forecast about capacity and coal replacement; numbers are rough and the argument is speculative.

title: Personal reflection on a neighbor's flowers
why: Nostalgic anecdote about a neighborhood losing character; reflective, with no lesson beyond personal observation.

title: Argument for returning to the office
why: Personal preference list about productivity, fitness and food; opinion, not generalizable evidence.

title: Additive versus aligning abstractions, and why they leak
why: Additive abstractions add capabilities to an underlying concept and tend to leak; aligning ones hide detail and model differently.

title: Company co-founder on lack of reviews
why: Vendor response explaining why few reviews exist and pitching its service; promotional rather than informative.

title: AngularJS providers exist for pre-start configuration
why: Providers are configured in config blocks via the Provider suffix before use; services and factories build instances differently.

title: List of April Fools' Day announcements
why: Link list and jokes about a fake MS-DOS phone OS; entertaining but offers no technical or lasting insight.

title: Frustration with Apple and attempts to switch
why: Venting about Apple hardware and failed alternatives; emotional rant without concrete guidance.

title: Complaints about Linux power management and displays
why: Personal experience and opinion about Linux laptop issues; grievances without a solution or deeper analysis.

title: Claimed insider view of Mt. Gox's insolvency plan
why: Describes an exchange-coordinated plan to transfer customers and shift blame to a bug story; account is unverified but detailed.

title: Argument on women in computing and stem
why: Opinion comparing field participation and the Google memo; contentious argument without decisive evidence.

title: Argument about state laws and constitutional precedent
why: Political analysis of court rulings and state power; advocacy rather than an informative explanation.

title: Practical advice for 501(c)(3) status for open source
why: Hire a nonprofit attorney rather than DIY, and explain copyleft to the IRS as public benefit, not private benefit to for-profits.

title: What standard technical interviews actually assess
why: Interviewers use standard problems to gauge how much hand-holding a candidate needs; strong candidates understand the purpose and think aloud.

title: Why interviews are a poor measure of engineers
why: Interviews are hostile and depleting, so their results reflect stress as much as skill; hiring should expect limited signal from one session.

title: Idea for voting on work emails
why: Product idea for email feedback widgets; a speculative suggestion without evidence or implementation insight.

title: Argument against using hate labels in politics
why: Political opinion about labels and discourse; argumentative and not technically informative.

title: Proposal for payment-aware web protocols
why: Speculative proposal that ads killed RSS and protocols should embed payment; an opinion piece without a worked design.

title: Why x86 complicates compilers and register allocation
why: Few registers, overlapping register classes, irregular encodings, and fixed multiply/divide registers all make register allocation harder.

title: Argument that cities should not fund stadiums
why: Policy opinion arguing stadium finance is bad but acknowledges public-utility arguments; mostly advocacy.

title: Personal account of thinking without words
why: First-person introspection about thinking without language; interesting perspective but subjective and unverified.

title: Defense of Washington Post reporting
why: Political argument about media reliability and a commenter; partisan, not informative.

title: Argument that bitcoin is worthless
why: Labor theory versus subjective value argument against bitcoin; advocacy with assertion, not evidence about markets.

title: Why developers over-invest in tooling
why: Like woodworkers building jigs, engineers enjoy internal tooling more than shipped products, which can hide software's productivity gains.

title: Why researchers must never dump user data
why: Exploits should stop at proof of existence; pivoting to dump sensitive data creates legal and employment risk for the researcher.

title: Argument against the 'can't hack it' stereotype
why: Opinion defending government workers; cites salary observations and rule constraints, but mostly argumentative.

title: Anecdote about passport verification for streaming
why: Personal experience of identity verification on a Chinese livestream app; a grievance with limited general lesson.

title: Argument that homework teaches kids time is worthless
why: Speculative psychological argument about busywork and instruments; opinion rather than evidence.

title: Canada versus US gun ownership and mass shootings
why: Canada's mass-shooting deaths per capita are about a third of the US's, yet track it once guns owned are controlled.

title: Five policy proposals for Occupy Wall Street
why: Political wish list on transparency, banking separation and transaction taxes; advocacy without detailed analysis.

title: Index fund fees matter less than starting now
why: A cheaper option saves about 0.09% a year, while delaying investing six months costs more; open a low-cost index account now.

title: Why studio innovation teams fail without authority
why: Innovation groups hired from tech lack P&L and mandate, sit in silos, and lose to internal fiefdoms that won't fund others' wins.

title: Comparing Gogs and Gitea by stars and features
why: Star counts and README feature lists are a shallow comparison; opinion about maintainers without technical depth.

title: Critique of startup culture and age
why: Opinion contrasting startup buzzwords with hardware-heavy industries; persuasive but mostly rhetorical.

title: Traits of strong teams that fire quickly
why: Management anecdote about strict expectations and quick terminations; a practical view, but a single-team experience.

title: Rating random statements for profundity
why: Playful critique of nonsense statements; entertaining but offers no technical or factual lesson.

title: Opinion that python 3 was a mistake
why: Argues Python 3 churn was for maintainers and slower; opinion-heavy with contested performance claims.

title: Critique of a list-style essay on poverty
why: Opinion on how people describe their hardship; emotional argument rather than informative content.

title: Anecdote comparing Linode and DigitalOcean latency
why: Personal hosting experience with a single traceroute; anecdotal and low generality.
